03 / WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES

A wiring map becomes
an experiment.

01

Load the wiring

The code reads a measured fly connectome: which neurons connect, and how many synaptic contacts link them. All 166,700 modeled neurons participate.

Connectome()
02

Let neurons respond

Each neuron is a simplified electrical unit. Input raises its voltage; crossing a threshold produces a spike that affects connected neurons.

build_brains(…)
03

Change one property

Lower a threshold, remove contacts, or silence cells. Replay the same input so the paired difference comes from the changed model condition.

thresholds · weights · silencing
04

Count the output

Deliver input to eight projection neurons, then count responses. Repeat with six input and damage seeds to see how variable the result is.

Brains.run(…)

04 / HOW TO TALK ABOUT THIS

Your explanation,
in plain language.

Use this as a starting point for a presentation.

“We used a whole-fly nervous-system model to ask how three amyloid-inspired changes affect neural signaling. Combined changes roughly halved the output response. Restoring contacts increased the response, but restoring excitability alone usually reduced it further. That tells us circuit changes interact: more firing does not automatically mean healthier function.”

The boundary: This experiment measures short circuit responses. It did not test learning, hours-long memory loss, amyloid chemistry or human Alzheimer’s disease. Parameter restoration is a model control, not a treatment result.

WHAT SURPRISED US

The baseline matters.

The original-graph comparator produced about 822 output spikes versus 11 in the published model. Adaptation and the removal of antennal-lobe connections strongly change the operating regime. Even the published model sometimes kept firing after input ended.

WHAT SUPPORTS THE WORK

Reproducible, with a defined scope.

54 published-model trials, 54 comparator trials, six successful full-restoration checks and 21 targeted automated tests. Saved inputs and damage draws make the comparisons auditable.
